h1.en: Health Insurance for California Gig Workers in 2026: AB5, Prop 22, and Medi-Cal
h1.es: Seguro Medico para Trabajadores Gig en California en 2026: AB5, Proposicion 22 y Medi-Cal

subhero.en: California rideshare and delivery drivers navigate a unique three-layer system in 2026: Proposition 22 healthcare stipends (up to $579/month), Medi-Cal for those earning under 138% FPL ($22,025 single), and Covered California marketplace plans with federal Premium Tax Credits phasing out at 400% FPL ($63,840 single). AB5 classifies most gig workers as independent contractors under Prop 22, meaning no employer-sponsored coverage but access to the stipend and self-employed tax tools.
subhero.es: Los conductores de viajes compartidos y de entrega en California navegan un sistema unico de tres capas en 2026: estipendios de salud de la Proposicion 22 (hasta $579/mes), Medi-Cal para quienes ganan menos del 138% FPL ($22,025 individual) y planes del mercado de Covered California con Creditos Fiscales de Prima federales que se eliminan al 400% FPL ($63,840 individual). AB5 clasifica a la mayoria de los trabajadores gig como contratistas independientes bajo la Prop 22, lo que significa que no tienen cobertura patrocinada por el empleador pero tienen acceso al estipendio y herramientas fiscales para trabajadores independientes.

quickAnswer.en: California gig workers, including Uber drivers, Lyft drivers, DoorDash drivers, and Instacart shoppers, have three main coverage paths in 2026. First, Medi-Cal (California's Medicaid program) covers any gig worker earning below 138% FPL ($22,025 for a single person) at no cost. Second, eligible app-based drivers who average 15 or more active hours per week qualify for the Proposition 22 healthcare stipend, worth up to approximately $579 per month in 2026, which can fund a Covered California plan. Third, independent contractors earning above 138% FPL can purchase a subsidized plan on Covered California using federal Premium Tax Credits (PTCs) if income stays below 400% FPL ($63,840 single). California also restored a state Premium Subsidy Program in 2026 for those at or below 165% FPL, partially offsetting the expiration of enhanced federal subsidies. The self-employment health insurance deduction (Form 7206) reduces income tax for gig workers with net self-employment income, and an HSA-qualified HDHP adds a triple tax advantage on top.
quickAnswer.es: Los trabajadores gig de California, incluyendo conductores de Uber, Lyft, DoorDash e Instacart, tienen tres caminos principales de cobertura en 2026. Primero, Medi-Cal (el programa Medicaid de California) cubre a cualquier trabajador gig que gane por debajo del 138% FPL ($22,025 para una persona sola) sin costo. Segundo, los conductores de plataformas que promedian 15 o mas horas activas por semana califican para el estipendio de salud de la Proposicion 22, que vale hasta aproximadamente $579 al mes en 2026. Tercero, los contratistas independientes que ganan mas del 138% FPL pueden comprar un plan subsidiado en Covered California usando Creditos Fiscales de Prima (PTC) federales si sus ingresos se mantienen bajo el 400% FPL ($63,840 individual). California tambien restituyo un Programa de Subsidio Estatal de Prima en 2026 para quienes estan en o por debajo del 165% FPL.

introParagraphs.en: California's Assembly Bill 5 (AB5), signed in September 2019, fundamentally changed how gig economy platforms classify their workers, applying the ABC test to determine whether a worker is an employee or an independent contractor. Proposition 22, passed by voters in November 2020, carved out an exemption for app-based rideshare and delivery companies, allowing Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, and Instacart to continue treating their drivers as independent contractors while requiring those platforms to offer alternative benefits, including a quarterly healthcare stipend. For California gig workers, rideshare drivers, delivery drivers, and other app-based independent contractors, understanding how AB5 and Proposition 22 interact with Medi-Cal, Covered California, and the federal Premium Tax Credit is the key to finding affordable health coverage in 2026.
introParagraphs.es: El Proyecto de Ley 5 de la Asamblea de California (AB5), promulgado en septiembre de 2019, cambio fundamentalmente como las plataformas de la economia gig clasifican a sus trabajadores, aplicando la prueba ABC para determinar si un trabajador es empleado o contratista independiente. La Proposicion 22, aprobada por los votantes en noviembre de 2020, creo una exencion para las empresas de viajes compartidos y entrega basadas en aplicaciones, permitiendo a Uber, Lyft, DoorDash e Instacart seguir tratando a sus conductores como contratistas independientes, mientras exige a esas plataformas ofrecer beneficios alternativos, incluido un estipendio trimestral de salud.

introParagraphs.en: California gig workers face a coverage picture that differs from freelancers in other states in two key ways. First, Covered California, California's state-run ACA marketplace, sets its own plan rules and subsidy architecture. In 2026, California launched a state Premium Subsidy Program that partially replaces the expired federal enhanced subsidies for enrollees at or below 165% FPL. Second, the Prop 22 stipend is a California-only benefit with no equivalent in other states: app-based drivers who meet the hours threshold receive a quarterly cash payment earmarked for health insurance premiums. This guide covers every layer: Medi-Cal eligibility, Prop 22 stipend mechanics, Covered California subsidy thresholds, the self-employed health insurance deduction (Form 7206), HSA options for 1099 contractors, and the Marketplace Special Enrollment Period triggers most relevant to California independent contractors.
introParagraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig de California enfrentan un panorama de cobertura que difiere de los freelancers en otros estados de dos maneras clave. Primero, Covered California, el mercado ACA gestionado por el estado, establece sus propias reglas de planes y arquitectura de subsidios. En 2026, California lanzo un Programa de Subsidio Estatal de Prima que reemplaza parcialmente los subsidios federales mejorados vencidos para los inscritos en o por debajo del 165% FPL. Segundo, el estipendio de la Prop 22 es un beneficio exclusivo de California sin equivalente en otros estados: los conductores de plataformas que cumplen el umbral de horas reciben un pago trimestral en efectivo destinado a las primas de seguro medico.

heading.en: Option 1: Medi-Cal, Free California Medicaid Coverage
heading.es: Opcion 1: Medi-Cal, Cobertura Medicaid Gratuita de California

paragraphs.en: Medi-Cal is California's Medicaid program and covers gig workers, rideshare drivers, delivery drivers, and other independent contractors who earn at or below 138% of the Federal Poverty Level. In 2026, that threshold is $22,025 per year for a single adult. Medi-Cal covers full medical, dental, and mental health services with no monthly premium and minimal or no cost sharing for most services. Gig workers calculate their income for Medi-Cal using net self-employment income, calculated as gross 1099 earnings minus allowable business expenses (mileage at $0.725/mile in 2026, phone, data, equipment). A DoorDash driver grossing $28,000 but deducting $6,000 in eligible expenses may land at a MAGI below $22,025 and qualify for Medi-Cal at no cost.
paragraphs.es: Medi-Cal es el programa Medicaid de California y cubre a trabajadores gig, conductores de viajes compartidos, conductores de entrega y otros contratistas independientes que ganan en o por debajo del 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza. En 2026, ese umbral es de $22,025 al ano para un adulto soltero. Medi-Cal cubre servicios medicos, dentales y de salud mental completos sin prima mensual y con costos minimos o nulos para la mayoria de los servicios. Los trabajadores gig calculan sus ingresos para Medi-Cal usando el ingreso neto del trabajo independiente: ganancias brutas 1099 menos los gastos comerciales permitidos.

paragraphs.en: California has expanded Medi-Cal to all income-eligible adults regardless of immigration status, though a January 2026 enrollment freeze stopped new enrollments for undocumented adults ages 19 and older who are not pregnant. Existing Medi-Cal enrollees who renew on time keep their coverage. App-based drivers who qualify for Medi-Cal should still report the Prop 22 stipend as income, though in most cases, the stipend is specifically excluded from Medi-Cal income calculations when used for its stated purpose of purchasing health insurance. Verify with Covered California (coveredca.com) or your county social services office. California gig workers can apply for Medi-Cal year-round through Covered California or BenefitsCal.com.
paragraphs.es: California ha ampliado Medi-Cal a todos los adultos elegibles por ingresos independientemente del estatus migratorio, aunque una suspension de inscripcion en enero de 2026 detiene nuevas inscripciones para adultos indocumentados de 19 anos o mas que no estan embarazadas. Los trabajadores gig que califican para Medi-Cal deben reportar el estipendio Prop 22 como ingreso, aunque en la mayoria de los casos el estipendio se excluye especificamente de los calculos de ingresos de Medi-Cal cuando se usa para su proposito declarado de comprar seguro medico.

heading.en: Option 2: Covered California Plan Funded by the Prop 22 Stipend
heading.es: Opcion 2: Plan de Covered California Financiado por el Estipendio de la Prop 22

paragraphs.en: California's Proposition 22 requires app-based rideshare and delivery companies, including Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart, and Postmates, to pay a quarterly healthcare stipend to eligible drivers. To qualify, a California app-based driver must average at least 15 active engaged hours per week over the calendar quarter and maintain proof of qualifying health insurance coverage. The 2026 stipend is based on the average statewide Covered California Bronze plan premium of $706 per month. Drivers averaging 25 or more active hours per week receive approximately $579 per month (82% of the bronze premium); drivers averaging 15 to 24 hours receive approximately $289 per month (41% of the bronze premium). Payments are made quarterly through the platform app.
paragraphs.es: La Proposicion 22 de California obliga a las empresas de viajes compartidos y entrega basadas en aplicaciones, incluyendo Uber, Lyft, DoorDash e Instacart, a pagar un estipendio trimestral de salud a los conductores elegibles. Para calificar, un conductor de plataforma en California debe promediar al menos 15 horas activas comprometidas por semana durante el trimestre calendario y mantener prueba de cobertura de seguro medico calificada. El estipendio de 2026 se basa en la prima promedio del plan Bronze de Covered California en todo el estado de $706 al mes.

paragraphs.en: The Prop 22 stipend is designed to fund a Covered California plan. A rideshare driver in the 138% to 400% FPL income band can pair the federal Premium Tax Credit (PTC) with the Prop 22 stipend for near-zero net premium on a Bronze or Silver plan. The stipend counts as income for federal PTC purposes, so drivers must factor it into their MAGI projection when estimating subsidy eligibility. Drivers above 400% FPL ($63,840 single in 2026) do not qualify for federal PTCs but can still receive the Prop 22 stipend and apply it to a full-price Covered California plan. The Prop 22 stipend does NOT count as wages subject to FICA or California SDI; it is treated as a taxable income supplement for the driver, not a wage.
paragraphs.es: El estipendio de la Prop 22 esta disenado para financiar un plan de Covered California. Un conductor de viajes compartidos en la banda de ingresos del 138% al 400% FPL puede combinar el Credito Fiscal de Prima (PTC) federal con el estipendio de la Prop 22 para obtener una prima neta casi nula en un plan Bronze o Silver. El estipendio cuenta como ingreso para los propositos del PTC federal, por lo que los conductores deben incluirlo en su proyeccion de MAGI al estimar la elegibilidad para subsidios.

heading.en: Option 3: Covered California with Federal Premium Tax Credit Only
heading.es: Opcion 3: Covered California con Credito Fiscal de Prima Federal Unicamente

paragraphs.en: California gig workers who do not qualify for the Prop 22 stipend (for example, TaskRabbit taskers, Handy handypeople, or freelancers not on app-based platforms covered by Prop 22) and whose income is between 138% FPL and 400% FPL can still access Covered California plans with federal Premium Tax Credits. The 2026 federal PTC is the standard income-based credit: subsidies phase down as income climbs toward 400% FPL ($63,840 single, $132,000 household of four) and stop entirely at 400%. An independent contractor at 200% FPL ($31,920 single) typically owes about 6.5% of income toward the benchmark Silver plan premium, with the federal PTC covering the rest. California's state Premium Subsidy Program additionally reduces premiums to near-zero for enrollees at or below 165% FPL ($26,334 single) by supplementing the federal credit.
paragraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig de California que no califican para el estipendio de la Prop 22 y cuyos ingresos estan entre el 138% FPL y el 400% FPL pueden acceder a planes de Covered California con Creditos Fiscales de Prima federales. El PTC federal de 2026 es el credito estandar basado en ingresos: los subsidios disminuyen a medida que los ingresos se acercan al 400% FPL ($63,840 individual, $132,000 para un hogar de cuatro) y se detienen completamente al 400%. El Programa de Subsidio Estatal de Prima de California reduce adicionalmente las primas a casi cero para los inscritos en o por debajo del 165% FPL.

paragraphs.en: When enrolling in Covered California as a 1099 contractor or independent contractor, project net income (not gross) for MAGI estimation. Net income is 1099 gross minus eligible business deductions (mileage, phone, equipment, home office). Covered California uses your annual projected MAGI. The marketplace distributes advance Premium Tax Credits monthly, and any over- or underpayment reconciles on Form 1095-A at tax time using IRS Form 8962. California gig workers should update Covered California within 30 days of any major income change, because underpaying credits creates a tax bill in April, and overpaying credits means leaving money on the table every month.
paragraphs.es: Al inscribirse en Covered California como contratista 1099, proyecte el ingreso neto (no bruto) para la estimacion del MAGI. El ingreso neto es el bruto 1099 menos las deducciones comerciales elegibles. Covered California usa su MAGI anual proyectado y distribuye Creditos Fiscales de Prima por adelantado mensualmente, con cualquier pago excesivo o insuficiente reconciliado en el Formulario 1095-A al momento de declarar impuestos.

heading.en: Option 4: HSA-Qualified HDHP for Higher-Earning Independent Contractors
heading.es: Opcion 4: HDHP Compatible con HSA para Contratistas Independientes de Mayores Ingresos

paragraphs.en: California gig workers and independent contractors earning above 400% FPL ($63,840 single, $132,000 for a family of four in 2026) no longer qualify for federal Premium Tax Credits. At this income level, an HSA-qualified High-Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) on Covered California becomes the most cost-effective structure. The 2026 HDHP minimum deductible is $1,700 self-only / $3,400 family. HDHPs typically carry the lowest sticker premiums among all metal-tier plans, and pairing one with a Health Savings Account (HSA) adds the triple tax advantage: contributions deduct above the line ($4,400 self / $8,750 family limit in 2026, plus $1,000 catch-up for those 55 and older), growth is tax-free, and qualified medical withdrawals are tax-free. A sole proprietor gig worker in the 24% federal bracket who maxes the self-only HSA saves approximately $1,056 in federal income tax, and the Form 7206 premium deduction stacks on top.
paragraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig y contratistas independientes de California que ganan por encima del 400% FPL ($63,840 individual, $132,000 para una familia de cuatro en 2026) ya no califican para los Creditos Fiscales de Prima federales. A este nivel de ingresos, un Plan de Deducible Alto (HDHP) compatible con HSA en Covered California es la estructura mas rentable. El deducible minimo del HDHP para 2026 es $1,700 individual / $3,400 familia. Combinar uno con una Cuenta de Ahorros para la Salud (HSA) agrega la ventaja fiscal triple.

heading.en: California Proposition 22 Healthcare Stipend: How It Works in 2026
heading.es: Estipendio de Salud de la Proposicion 22 de California: Como Funciona en 2026

paragraphs.en: California's Proposition 22 (passed November 3, 2020, effective January 1, 2021) requires app-based network companies to provide a quarterly healthcare stipend to eligible drivers and delivery workers. The platforms covered include Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart, Postmates, and other Prop 22-covered gig economy companies. To qualify, a California rideshare driver or delivery driver must average 15 or more active engaged hours per week during the calendar quarter and maintain qualifying health insurance coverage for the entire quarter. The stipend is calculated based on the average statewide monthly Covered California Bronze plan premium, which is $706 per month for 2026.
paragraphs.es: La Proposicion 22 de California (aprobada el 3 de noviembre de 2020, efectiva el 1 de enero de 2021) requiere que las companias de redes basadas en aplicaciones proporcionen un estipendio trimestral de salud a los conductores y trabajadores de entrega elegibles. Las plataformas cubiertas incluyen Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart y otras companias de la economia gig cubiertas por la Prop 22.

paragraphs.en: For 2026, the Prop 22 stipend tiers for California app-based drivers are: drivers averaging 25 or more active hours per week receive approximately $579 per month (paid quarterly as approximately $1,737); drivers averaging 15 to 24 hours per week receive approximately $289 per month (paid quarterly as approximately $867). These amounts represent 82% and 41% respectively of the $706 monthly 2026 Covered California Bronze benchmark premium. Drivers submit proof of health insurance coverage through the platform app each quarter. The stipend is paid directly to the driver, who uses it to fund premiums on any qualifying plan: Covered California, spouse employer plan, COBRA, or Medicare. Covered California's Prop 22 Quick Guide for Enrollers (coveredca.com) details the exact submission process.
paragraphs.es: Para 2026, los niveles del estipendio Prop 22 para conductores de plataformas en California son: conductores que promedian 25 o mas horas activas por semana reciben aproximadamente $579 al mes (pagado trimestralmente como aproximadamente $1,737); conductores que promedian 15 a 24 horas por semana reciben aproximadamente $289 al mes (pagado trimestralmente como aproximadamente $867). Estos montos representan el 82% y 41% respectivamente de la prima de referencia Bronze de Covered California de $706 al mes para 2026.

paragraphs.en: National Equity Atlas research shows that as of 2023, fewer than 40% of eligible California rideshare drivers were actually claiming the Prop 22 stipend, leaving hundreds of millions of dollars in unclaimed quarterly payments. The most common reasons drivers miss the stipend: not knowing about the program, failing to submit proof of coverage within the quarter, or having inconsistent hours that drop below the 15-hour threshold. California app-based drivers who meet the hours requirement should treat claiming the Prop 22 stipend as their first financial health insurance step, before calculating Covered California subsidies.
paragraphs.es: La investigacion del Atlas Nacional de Equidad muestra que, a partir de 2023, menos del 40% de los conductores de viajes compartidos elegibles en California reclamaban el estipendio de la Prop 22, dejando cientos de millones de dolares en pagos trimestrales no reclamados. Los conductores de plataformas en California que cumplen el requisito de horas deben tratar de reclamar el estipendio Prop 22 como su primer paso financiero de seguro medico.

heading.en: Premium Tax Credit (PTC) Eligibility for California Gig Workers in 2026
heading.es: Elegibilidad para el Credito Fiscal de Prima (PTC) para Trabajadores Gig de California en 2026

paragraphs.en: California gig workers, rideshare drivers, and independent contractors projecting their 2026 Covered California eligibility need one critical number: 400% of the Federal Poverty Level. For 2026, that is $63,840 for a single adult and $132,000 for a household of four. Below that ceiling, the Premium Tax Credit (PTC) is available and phases down as income climbs. Subsidies do not snap off at 200% or 300% FPL; they get progressively smaller at each income step, reaching zero at exactly 400% FPL. Above 400%, a California gig worker pays the full benchmark premium with no federal help. The 2026 subsidy cliff is real: the enhanced subsidies from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA, signed March 11, 2021) and the Inflation Reduction Act (signed August 16, 2022) expired January 1, 2026.
paragraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig, conductores de viajes compartidos y contratistas independientes de California que proyectan su elegibilidad para Covered California 2026 necesitan un numero critico: el 400% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza. Para 2026, eso es $63,840 para un adulto soltero y $132,000 para un hogar de cuatro personas. Por debajo de ese techo, el Credito Fiscal de Prima (PTC) esta disponible y disminuye a medida que los ingresos suben. Los subsidios no desaparecen abruptamente al 200% o 300% FPL; se reducen progresivamente en cada paso de ingresos, llegando a cero exactamente al 400% FPL.

paragraphs.en: California added a state-funded Premium Subsidy Program in 2026 that specifically targets enrollees at or below 165% FPL. At 150% FPL and below, the state subsidy maintains near-zero premiums (similar to what enhanced federal credits provided through 2025). At 150% to 165% FPL, a partial state subsidy reduces premiums. Above 165% FPL, California gig workers rely entirely on the federal PTC until the 400% FPL cliff. This means a 1099 contractor earning between 165% and 400% FPL ($26,334 to $63,840 single) faces the full brunt of the enhanced-subsidy expiration in 2026. Premiums in that band rose substantially compared to 2025. A Covered California Silver plan for a 35-year-old at 300% FPL may run $250 to $400 per month after the federal PTC in 2026.
paragraphs.es: California agrego un Programa de Subsidio Estatal de Prima en 2026 que se dirige especificamente a los inscritos en o por debajo del 165% FPL. Por encima del 165% FPL, los trabajadores gig de California dependen completamente del PTC federal hasta el limite del 400% FPL. Esto significa que un contratista 1099 que gana entre el 165% y el 400% FPL enfrenta el impacto total de la expiracion del subsidio mejorado en 2026.

paragraphs.en: MAGI for Covered California purposes is net self-employment income plus any other income sources. For an app-based driver, MAGI is: gross 1099 platform earnings, minus eligible business deductions (mileage at $0.725/mile in 2026, cell phone, car insurance allocated to business use, equipment, data), minus half of self-employment tax (the deductible SE tax portion), minus the self-employed health insurance deduction (Form 7206), plus the Prop 22 stipend received. Note: the Prop 22 stipend is typically included in MAGI for PTC purposes. An Uber driver grossing $40,000 with $8,000 in deductions, $2,500 in SE tax half-deduction, and $6,000 in premiums (Form 7206) could land at a MAGI near $23,500, inside the Medi-Cal threshold, triggering a mid-year plan change. Covered California can be updated at any time to reflect income changes.
paragraphs.es: El MAGI para los propositos de Covered California es el ingreso neto del trabajo independiente mas cualquier otra fuente de ingresos. Para un conductor de plataforma, el MAGI es: ganancias brutas 1099 de la plataforma, menos deducciones comerciales elegibles (kilometraje a $0.725/milla en 2026, telefono celular, seguro de automovil asignado al uso comercial, equipo, datos), menos la mitad del impuesto al trabajo independiente, menos la deduccion de seguro medico (Formulario 7206), mas el estipendio Prop 22 recibido.

list.en: Below 138% FPL ($22,025 single in 2026): Medi-Cal, no premium
list.es: Por debajo del 138% FPL ($22,025 individual en 2026): Medi-Cal, sin prima

list.en: 138% to 165% FPL ($22,025 to $26,334 single): federal PTC + California state Premium Subsidy (near-zero premium at 150% and below)
list.es: 138% a 165% FPL ($22,025 a $26,334 individual): PTC federal + Subsidio Estatal de Prima de California (prima casi nula al 150% y por debajo)

list.en: 165% to 250% FPL ($26,334 to $39,900 single): federal PTC; Silver plans with Cost-Sharing Reductions (CSRs) available for maximum value
list.es: 165% a 250% FPL ($26,334 a $39,900 individual): PTC federal; planes Silver con Reducciones de Costos Compartidos (CSRs) disponibles para valor maximo

list.en: 250% to 400% FPL ($39,900 to $63,840 single): federal PTC phases down; premiums climb steeply above 350% FPL
list.es: 250% a 400% FPL ($39,900 a $63,840 individual): PTC federal disminuye; las primas suben considerablemente por encima del 350% FPL

list.en: Above 400% FPL ($63,840 single): no federal PTC, no California state subsidy; full-price Covered California plans only
list.es: Por encima del 400% FPL ($63,840 individual): sin PTC federal, sin subsidio estatal de California; solo planes de Covered California a precio completo

heading.en: 2026 Medi-Cal and Covered California Income Thresholds for California Gig Workers by Household Size
heading.es: Umbrales de Ingresos de Medi-Cal y Covered California 2026 para Trabajadores Gig de California por Tamano del Hogar

paragraphs.en: California gig workers, rideshare drivers, DoorDash drivers, and independent contractors use the table below to find their income bracket. Medi-Cal covers anyone below 138% FPL. Covered California federal PTC subsidies phase down between 138% and 400% FPL and stop above 400%. All figures are 2026 annual MAGI (net self-employment income, not gross). The California state Premium Subsidy Program additionally supports enrollees below 165% FPL in 2026.
paragraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig, conductores de viajes compartidos, conductores de DoorDash y contratistas independientes de California usan la tabla a continuacion para encontrar su banda de ingresos. Medi-Cal cubre a cualquier persona por debajo del 138% FPL. Los subsidios PTC federales de Covered California disminuyen entre el 138% y el 400% FPL y se detienen por encima del 400%. Todas las cifras son MAGI anual 2026.

caption.es: Limites de Ingresos Medi-Cal (138% FPL) y Limite de Subsidio Covered California (400% FPL) 2026 por Tamano del Hogar

footnote.en: Income is annual net MAGI (gross 1099 earnings minus business deductions, minus half of SE tax, minus Form 7206 premium deduction). The Prop 22 stipend is counted as income for federal PTC purposes. The California state Premium Subsidy Program additionally supports enrollees at or below 165% FPL ($26,334 single, $54,450 household of four). Source: HHS ASPE 2026 Poverty Guidelines; CoveredCA.com FPL Chart.
footnote.es: El ingreso es el MAGI neto anual (ganancias brutas 1099 menos deducciones comerciales, menos la mitad del impuesto SE, menos la deduccion de primas del Formulario 7206). El estipendio Prop 22 se cuenta como ingreso para los propositos del PTC federal. Fuente: Directrices de Pobreza ASPE HHS 2026; Tabla FPL de CoveredCA.com.

heading.en: Self-Employment Health Insurance Deduction (Form 7206) for California Gig Workers
heading.es: Deduccion de Seguro Medico para Trabajadores Independientes (Formulario 7206) para Trabajadores Gig de California

paragraphs.en: Form 7206 lets California gig workers, independent contractors, and sole proprietors deduct 100% of health insurance premiums paid for themselves, their spouse, and dependents as an above-the-line adjustment on Schedule 1, line 17 of Form 1040. This deduction reduces federal income tax and California state income tax. Crucially, Form 7206 reduces income tax only; it does NOT reduce self-employment tax calculated on Schedule SE. The 15.3% self-employment tax (12.4% Social Security plus 2.9% Medicare) is calculated on net self-employment earnings before the health insurance deduction is applied. The deduction flows from Form 7206 to Schedule 1 to Form 1040 but does not touch Schedule SE at any point.
paragraphs.es: El Formulario 7206 permite a los trabajadores gig, contratistas independientes y propietarios unicos de California deducir el 100% de las primas de seguro medico pagadas por ellos mismos, su conyuge y dependientes como ajuste sobre la linea en el Schedule 1, linea 17 del Formulario 1040. Esta deduccion reduce el impuesto sobre la renta federal y el impuesto estatal de California. El Formulario 7206 reduce el impuesto sobre la renta solamente; NO reduce el impuesto al trabajo independiente calculado en el Schedule SE.

paragraphs.en: For a 1099 contractor or DoorDash driver paying $400 per month in Covered California premiums ($4,800 annually), the Form 7206 deduction at the 22% federal bracket saves approximately $1,056 in federal income tax per year. Combined with California's 9.3% state income tax bracket (for income above $66,296 single), the total income tax savings approach $1,502. Additionally, the Form 7206 deduction lowers MAGI, which can move the driver into a higher subsidy band for the following tax year. Two limits apply: (1) the deduction cannot exceed net SE earnings minus half of SE tax; and (2) any month during which the contractor or their spouse was eligible for an employer-sponsored plan disqualifies that month's premium from the deduction. Most app-based California gig workers who have no employer coverage available qualify for the full deduction every month.
paragraphs.es: Para un contratista 1099 o conductor de DoorDash que paga $400 al mes en primas de Covered California ($4,800 anuales), la deduccion del Formulario 7206 al rango federal del 22% ahorra aproximadamente $1,056 en impuesto sobre la renta federal por ano. Ademas, la deduccion del Formulario 7206 reduce el MAGI, lo que puede mover al conductor a una banda de subsidio mas alta para el siguiente ano fiscal.

heading.en: HSA and HDHP Fit for California Gig Workers in 2026
heading.es: Compatibilidad de HSA y HDHP para Trabajadores Gig de California en 2026

paragraphs.en: California gig workers and independent contractors enrolled in an HSA-qualified High-Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) can open and contribute to a Health Savings Account (HSA). For 2026, an HDHP must have a minimum deductible of $1,700 for self-only coverage or $3,400 for family coverage. The 2026 HSA contribution limit is $4,400 for self-only coverage and $8,750 for family coverage, plus a $1,000 catch-up contribution for those age 55 and older. HSA contributions offer the triple tax advantage: contributions are deductible above the line (reducing income tax and MAGI), growth is tax-free inside the account, and qualified medical withdrawals are completely tax-free. After age 65, HSA funds can be withdrawn for any purpose without penalty, functioning like a Traditional IRA.
paragraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig e independientes de California inscritos en un Plan de Deducible Alto (HDHP) compatible con HSA pueden abrir y contribuir a una Cuenta de Ahorros para la Salud (HSA). Para 2026, un HDHP debe tener un deducible minimo de $1,700 para cobertura individual o $3,400 para cobertura familiar. El limite de contribucion al HSA para 2026 es $4,400 para cobertura individual y $8,750 para cobertura familiar, mas una contribucion adicional de $1,000 para los mayores de 55 anos.

paragraphs.en: A Flexible Spending Account (FSA) is an employer-sponsored benefit only. Most California gig workers, DoorDash drivers, Instacart shoppers, and other app-based independent contractors do NOT have access to an FSA because Prop 22 classified them as independent contractors, not employees. FSA is not an option for 1099 contractors on the Covered California marketplace. The HSA is the tax-advantaged medical savings vehicle available to California independent contractors, but only when paired with a qualifying HDHP. A Covered California Bronze HDHP is the most common vehicle for opening an HSA. Not all Covered California HDHP plans are HSA-qualified; check for the explicit 'HSA-compatible' label when comparing plans.
paragraphs.es: Una Cuenta de Gastos Flexibles (FSA) es un beneficio exclusivo del empleador. La mayoria de los trabajadores gig, conductores de DoorDash, compradores de Instacart y otros contratistas independientes basados en aplicaciones en California NO tienen acceso a una FSA porque la Prop 22 los clasifico como contratistas independientes, no como empleados. El HSA es el instrumento de ahorro medico con ventajas fiscales disponible para los contratistas independientes de California, pero solo cuando se combina con un HDHP calificado.

heading.en: Marketplace Special Enrollment Period (SEP) Triggers for California Gig Workers
heading.es: Activadores del Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) del Mercado para Trabajadores Gig de California

paragraphs.en: Covered California open enrollment runs November 1 through January 31 each year for coverage starting the following February (or January 15 for January 1 coverage). Outside open enrollment, California gig workers can enroll in a Covered California plan only if they qualify for a Marketplace Special Enrollment Period. A Marketplace SEP opens a 60-day window from the date of the qualifying event. California has some of the most generous SEP rules in the country, including a year-round Medi-Cal enrollment pathway and a Special Enrollment Period for income changes that cross the Medi-Cal threshold.
paragraphs.es: La inscripcion abierta de Covered California se extiende del 1 de noviembre al 31 de enero de cada ano para cobertura que comienza en febrero siguiente. Fuera de la inscripcion abierta, los trabajadores gig de California solo pueden inscribirse en un plan de Covered California si califican para un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial del Mercado. Un SEP del mercado abre una ventana de 60 dias desde la fecha del evento calificador.

paragraphs.en: California gig workers transitioning between Medi-Cal and Covered California should be aware of the income-change SEP: if income rises above 138% FPL mid-year (moving out of Medi-Cal), a Covered California SEP opens. Conversely, if income drops below 138% FPL, a Medi-Cal SEP opens and Covered California enrollment can be terminated. For a rideshare driver or delivery driver with variable earnings, this income-change SEP is the most common trigger. Track income monthly and contact Covered California at coveredca.com or 1-800-300-1506 within 60 days of any qualifying event.
paragraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig de California que hacen la transicion entre Medi-Cal y Covered California deben conocer el SEP de cambio de ingresos: si los ingresos suben por encima del 138% FPL a mitad de ano (saliendo de Medi-Cal), se abre un SEP de Covered California. Para un conductor de viajes compartidos o conductor de entrega con ingresos variables, este SEP de cambio de ingresos es el activador mas comun.

list.en: Loss of other coverage (losing Medi-Cal, losing coverage from a family member's plan, end of COBRA): 60-day SEP window
list.es: Perdida de otra cobertura (perder Medi-Cal, perder la cobertura del plan de un familiar, fin de COBRA): ventana SEP de 60 dias

heading.en: How to Apply for Health Insurance as a California Gig Worker in 2026
heading.es: Como Solicitar Seguro Medico como Trabajador Gig en California en 2026

paragraphs.en: California gig workers, rideshare drivers, and delivery drivers can apply for Medi-Cal and Covered California through the same portal: coveredca.com or by calling 1-800-300-1506. Medi-Cal enrollment is year-round; Covered California open enrollment runs November 1 through January 31. The application asks for projected annual net income, household size, immigration status, and current coverage status. Medi-Cal eligibility is determined immediately in most cases; Covered California plan selection follows income verification. The state-run portal integrates both programs and routes applicants to the right coverage automatically based on income.
paragraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig, conductores de viajes compartidos y conductores de entrega de California pueden solicitar Medi-Cal y Covered California a traves del mismo portal: coveredca.com o llamando al 1-800-300-1506. La inscripcion a Medi-Cal es durante todo el ano; la inscripcion abierta de Covered California se extiende del 1 de noviembre al 31 de enero.

list.en: Step 1: Visit coveredca.com or call 1-800-300-1506. Create or log into your Covered California account.
list.es: Paso 1: Visita coveredca.com o llama al 1-800-300-1506. Crea o inicia sesion en tu cuenta de Covered California.

list.en: Step 2: Enter household size, projected 2026 net self-employment income (gross 1099 minus business expenses), and any other income sources including the Prop 22 stipend.
list.es: Paso 2: Ingresa el tamano del hogar, el ingreso neto proyectado del trabajo independiente para 2026 (bruto 1099 menos gastos comerciales) y cualquier otra fuente de ingresos incluyendo el estipendio Prop 22.

list.en: Step 3: The system routes to Medi-Cal (if income is below 138% FPL) or to Covered California plan selection (138-400% FPL) or full-price plan shopping (above 400% FPL).
list.es: Paso 3: El sistema te dirige a Medi-Cal (si los ingresos estan por debajo del 138% FPL) o a la seleccion de planes de Covered California (138-400% FPL) o a la compra de planes a precio completo (por encima del 400% FPL).

list.en: Step 4: If selecting a Covered California plan, compare Bronze (lowest premium, HSA-compatible), Silver (CSRs available below 250% FPL), Gold (rich benefits, higher premium), and Catastrophic (under 30 or hardship exemption only).
list.es: Paso 4: Si seleccionas un plan de Covered California, compara Bronze (prima mas baja, compatible con HSA), Silver (CSRs disponibles bajo 250% FPL), Gold (beneficios ricos, prima mas alta) y Catastrofico (solo para menores de 30 anos o exencion por dificultad).

list.en: Step 5: Confirm enrollment. You will receive a Form 1095-A from Covered California in January showing advance PTC amounts. Use Form 1095-A and IRS Form 8962 to reconcile credits at tax time.
list.es: Paso 5: Confirma la inscripcion. Recibiras un Formulario 1095-A de Covered California en enero que muestra los montos del PTC anticipado. Usa el Formulario 1095-A y el Formulario IRS 8962 para reconciliar los creditos al momento de declarar impuestos.

heading.en: Catastrophic Plan Eligibility for California Gig Workers
heading.es: Elegibilidad para Planes Catastroficos para Trabajadores Gig de California

paragraphs.en: Catastrophic health plans on the Covered California marketplace are available to California gig workers who are (a) under age 30, or (b) any age with a hardship exemption (for instance, a gig worker who cannot afford any marketplace plan, a homeless individual, or someone with unpaid medical debt exceeding a certain threshold). The 2026 catastrophic plan deductible equals the ACA marketplace out-of-pocket maximum: $10,600 for individual coverage. After the deductible is met, the plan covers all essential health benefits at no cost. Catastrophic plans on Covered California do NOT qualify for the Premium Tax Credit, so the premium is paid entirely out of pocket; premiums are typically $150 to $350 per month for adults under 30.
paragraphs.es: Los planes de salud catastroficos en el mercado de Covered California estan disponibles para los trabajadores gig de California que son (a) menores de 30 anos, o (b) de cualquier edad con una exencion por dificultad. El deducible del plan catastrofico de 2026 es igual al maximo de bolsillo del mercado ACA: $10,600 para cobertura individual. Los planes catastroficos en Covered California NO califican para el Credito Fiscal de Prima.

paragraphs.en: California gig workers over age 30 without a documented hardship exemption are NOT eligible for catastrophic plans on the Covered California marketplace. A 35-year-old rideshare driver looking for the cheapest possible plan should compare a Bronze HDHP (eligible for HSA, eligible for PTC subsidies if income qualifies) rather than a catastrophic plan. For under-30 independent contractors, the catastrophic plan makes sense only if income is above the 400% FPL cliff and an HSA-qualified Bronze HDHP premium would be similar or higher, which is rare but possible in higher-cost California counties.
paragraphs.es: Los trabajadores gig de California mayores de 30 anos sin una exencion por dificultad documentada NO son elegibles para planes catastroficos en el mercado de Covered California. Un conductor de viajes compartidos de 35 anos que busca el plan mas barato posible debe comparar un HDHP Bronze (elegible para HSA, elegible para subsidios PTC si los ingresos califican) en lugar de un plan catastrofico.

en.question: What is the cheapest health insurance for California gig workers in 2026?
en.answer: For California gig workers earning below $22,025 (single) in 2026, Medi-Cal is free with no premium. For app-based rideshare drivers and delivery drivers working 15 or more hours per week, the Prop 22 stipend (up to approximately $579/month in 2026) can fund most or all of a Covered California Bronze or Silver plan premium. Independent contractors between 138% and 400% FPL can access federal Premium Tax Credits through Covered California, with California's state Premium Subsidy Program providing additional support at or below 165% FPL. Above 400% FPL ($63,840 single), the cheapest option is usually a Covered California Bronze HDHP paired with a Health Savings Account.

en.question: Do California gig workers qualify for the Premium Tax Credit?
en.answer: Yes, if annual net MAGI is between 138% and 400% FPL. For a single California gig worker in 2026, that is $22,025 to $63,840. Net MAGI is gross 1099 income minus business deductions (mileage at $0.725/mile in 2026, phone, equipment) minus half of self-employment tax, minus Form 7206 health insurance premiums, plus the Prop 22 stipend if received. The federal Premium Tax Credit (PTC) phases down as income approaches 400% FPL and stops at $63,840 for a single person. California's state Premium Subsidy Program provides additional help for those at or below 165% FPL ($26,334 single) in 2026.

en.question: Can California gig workers deduct health insurance premiums on taxes?
en.answer: Yes, if they have net self-employment income and were not eligible for employer-sponsored coverage in a given month. Form 7206 lets app-based drivers, independent contractors, and sole proprietors deduct 100% of health insurance premiums above the line, reducing federal and California state income tax. Important: Form 7206 reduces income tax only. It does NOT reduce the 15.3% self-employment tax on Schedule SE. The 15.3% SE tax (Social Security plus Medicare) is calculated on net earnings before the health insurance premium deduction. California gig workers often misunderstand this: the Form 7206 benefit is real and valuable, but it does not cut SE tax.

en.question: How does the Prop 22 healthcare stipend work in 2026?
en.answer: California's Proposition 22 requires app-based platforms including Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, and Instacart to pay a quarterly healthcare stipend to eligible drivers. In 2026, the stipend is calculated as a percentage of the $706 average monthly Covered California Bronze premium: approximately $579/month (82%) for drivers averaging 25 or more active hours per week, and approximately $289/month (41%) for drivers averaging 15 to 24 hours per week. To receive the stipend, you must average the qualifying hours and submit proof of health insurance coverage through your platform app within each calendar quarter. The stipend counts as taxable income and as MAGI for Covered California subsidy calculations.

en.question: Can California gig workers use a Health Savings Account (HSA)?
en.answer: Yes, if enrolled in a qualifying HSA-compatible HDHP. For 2026, the HDHP minimum deductible is $1,700 for self-only or $3,400 for family. The HSA contribution limit in 2026 is $4,400 (self-only) or $8,750 (family), plus a $1,000 catch-up for those 55 or older. HSA contributions are deductible above the line, growth is tax-free, and qualified medical withdrawals are tax-free (the triple tax advantage). A Flexible Spending Account (FSA) is employer-only and is NOT available to California independent contractors, rideshare drivers, or delivery drivers classified as non-employees under Proposition 22. The HSA is the tax-advantaged medical savings account available to California gig workers.

en.question: What happens if a California gig worker earns too much for subsidies?
en.answer: California gig workers earning above 400% FPL ($63,840 single, $132,000 for a household of four in 2026) receive zero federal Premium Tax Credits. The enhanced subsidies from ARPA and the Inflation Reduction Act expired January 1, 2026. At that income level, the most tax-efficient strategy is a Covered California Bronze HDHP paired with a maxed HSA ($4,400 self / $8,750 family). The Form 7206 deduction still applies to reduce income tax, and the HSA triple tax advantage layers on top. Earning $1 above the 400% FPL cliff can cost thousands in lost subsidies. Gig workers near the threshold should time HSA contributions, retirement plan contributions (SEP-IRA, Solo 401k), and Form 7206 premium deductions to stay below the cliff.

en.question: When can California gig workers enroll in Covered California outside open enrollment?
en.answer: Outside the November 1 to January 31 open enrollment window, California gig workers can enroll through a Marketplace Special Enrollment Period (SEP). The most common SEP triggers for rideshare drivers and delivery drivers are: income change crossing the 138% FPL Medi-Cal threshold (either direction), loss of other coverage, marriage or divorce, birth or adoption of a child, moving to a new California county, or turning 26 and losing parent's coverage. Each SEP opens a 60-day window from the date of the qualifying event. Medi-Cal enrollment is available year-round at coveredca.com with no SEP required. Call 1-800-300-1506 or visit coveredca.com to report a qualifying event and open a SEP.

en.question: Does California's AB5 affect health insurance options for gig workers?
en.answer: AB5 established the ABC employment classification test for most California workers, which would have classified many gig workers as employees entitled to employer health benefits. However, Proposition 22 (passed November 2020) exempted app-based rideshare and delivery drivers from the AB5 ABC test, maintaining their independent contractor status. As a result, Uber drivers, Lyft drivers, DoorDash drivers, and Instacart shoppers remain independent contractors under California law, with no employer-sponsored health insurance but with access to the Prop 22 healthcare stipend. Gig workers not covered by Prop 22 (for example, TaskRabbit or independent freelancers) may be classified as employees under AB5 depending on the ABC test, potentially gaining access to employer health benefits.

es.question: ¿Cual es el seguro medico mas barato para los trabajadores gig de California en 2026?
es.answer: Para trabajadores gig de California que ganan menos de $22,025 (individual) en 2026, Medi-Cal es gratuito sin prima. Para los conductores de plataformas que trabajan 15 o mas horas por semana, el estipendio Prop 22 (hasta aproximadamente $579/mes en 2026) puede financiar la mayor parte o la totalidad de la prima de un plan Bronze o Silver de Covered California. Los contratistas independientes entre el 138% y el 400% FPL pueden acceder a Creditos Fiscales de Prima federales a traves de Covered California, con el Programa de Subsidio Estatal de Prima de California que brinda apoyo adicional al 165% FPL o por debajo.

es.question: ¿Los trabajadores gig de California califican para el Credito Fiscal de Prima?
es.answer: Si, si el MAGI neto anual esta entre el 138% y el 400% FPL. Para un trabajador gig soltero en California en 2026, eso es de $22,025 a $63,840. El MAGI neto es el ingreso bruto 1099 menos las deducciones comerciales menos la mitad del impuesto al trabajo independiente, menos las primas de seguro medico del Formulario 7206, mas el estipendio Prop 22 si se recibe. El Credito Fiscal de Prima (PTC) federal disminuye a medida que los ingresos se acercan al 400% FPL y se detiene en $63,840 para una persona soltera.

es.question: ¿Pueden los trabajadores gig de California deducir las primas de seguro medico en los impuestos?
es.answer: Si, si tienen ingreso neto del trabajo independiente y no eran elegibles para cobertura patrocinada por el empleador en un mes determinado. El Formulario 7206 permite a los conductores, contratistas independientes y propietarios unicos deducir el 100% de las primas de seguro medico por encima de la linea, reduciendo el impuesto sobre la renta federal y el estatal de California. Importante: el Formulario 7206 reduce el impuesto sobre la renta solamente. NO reduce el impuesto al trabajo independiente del 15.3% en el Schedule SE.

es.question: ¿Como funciona el estipendio de salud Prop 22 en 2026?
es.answer: La Proposicion 22 de California requiere que las plataformas basadas en aplicaciones incluyendo Uber, Lyft, DoorDash e Instacart paguen un estipendio trimestral de salud a los conductores elegibles. En 2026, el estipendio es de aproximadamente $579/mes (82%) para conductores que promedian 25 o mas horas activas por semana, y aproximadamente $289/mes (41%) para conductores que promedian 15 a 24 horas por semana, basado en la prima Bronze promedio de $706 al mes de Covered California. El estipendio cuenta como ingreso imponible y como MAGI para los calculos de subsidios de Covered California.

es.question: ¿Pueden los trabajadores gig de California usar una Cuenta de Ahorros para la Salud (HSA)?
es.answer: Si, si estan inscritos en un HDHP compatible con HSA que califique. Para 2026, el deducible minimo del HDHP es $1,700 para cobertura individual o $3,400 para familia. El limite de contribucion al HSA en 2026 es $4,400 (individual) o $8,750 (familia), mas $1,000 adicional para los mayores de 55 anos. Una Cuenta de Gastos Flexibles (FSA) es solo para empleadores y NO esta disponible para los contratistas independientes, conductores de viajes compartidos o conductores de entrega clasificados como no empleados bajo la Proposicion 22.

es.question: ¿Que pasa si un trabajador gig de California gana demasiado para los subsidios?
es.answer: Los trabajadores gig de California que ganan por encima del 400% FPL ($63,840 individual, $132,000 para un hogar de cuatro en 2026) no reciben Creditos Fiscales de Prima federales. Los subsidios mejorados de ARPA y la Ley de Reduccion de la Inflacion vencieron el 1 de enero de 2026. A ese nivel de ingresos, la estrategia mas eficiente fiscalmente es un HDHP Bronze de Covered California combinado con un HSA maximizado ($4,400 individual / $8,750 familia). La deduccion del Formulario 7206 todavia aplica para reducir el impuesto sobre la renta, y la ventaja fiscal triple del HSA se aplica encima.

es.question: ¿Cuando pueden los trabajadores gig de California inscribirse en Covered California fuera de la inscripcion abierta?
es.answer: Fuera de la ventana de inscripcion abierta del 1 de noviembre al 31 de enero, los trabajadores gig de California pueden inscribirse a traves de un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) del Mercado. Los activadores de SEP mas comunes para conductores de viajes compartidos y conductores de entrega son: cambio de ingresos que cruza el umbral de Medi-Cal del 138% FPL, perdida de otra cobertura, matrimonio o divorcio, nacimiento o adopcion de un hijo, mudanza a un nuevo condado de California, o cumplir 26 anos y perder la cobertura de los padres. Cada SEP abre una ventana de 60 dias desde la fecha del evento calificador.

es.question: ¿Como afecta el AB5 de California las opciones de seguro medico para los trabajadores gig?
es.answer: AB5 establecio la prueba ABC de clasificacion laboral para la mayoria de los trabajadores de California, lo que habria clasificado a muchos trabajadores gig como empleados con derecho a beneficios de salud del empleador. Sin embargo, la Proposicion 22 (aprobada en noviembre de 2020) exento a los conductores de viajes compartidos y entrega basados en aplicaciones de la prueba ABC de AB5, manteniendo su estatus de contratistas independientes. Como resultado, los conductores de Uber, Lyft, DoorDash e Instacart siguen siendo contratistas independientes bajo la ley de California, sin seguro medico patrocinado por el empleador pero con acceso al estipendio de salud Prop 22.
